chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Zakat al-Fitr is due on every head from your family, the small and the large, the free and the slave, the rich and the poor; for every person, half a sa' of wheat or barley, or a full sa' of dates or raisins, for the poor of the Muslims.
And he said: 'Dates are more beloved to me of those [options].'
And that which indicates what we have interpreted these hadiths as meaning is that the intended meaning is recommendation (nadhb) rather than obligation (ijab).

key_terms.صَاعٌ: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific amounts and types of food required for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that Zakat al-Fitr is obligatory on every individual—regardless of age, freedom, or wealth—with prescribed measures of half a sa' for grains or a full sa' for dates and raisins. The narration highlights a prophetic preference for dates, while the accompanying scholarly analysis clarifies that the underlying obligation is often interpreted as recommended (mandub) rather than strictly compulsory in certain contexts, reflecting the nuanced juristic discourse in Shia fiqh.
